- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.2) and prices are falling, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% to avoid missing downward momentum.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); apply a 1–3 day lag correction by smoothing out the peak.  
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.3–0.7) and price is trending, model often fails to capture mean reversion; add a 1–2 day mean-reversion buffer toward prior 10-day average.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to be overly optimistic in early periods (first 5–7 days); apply a downward bias of 1–3% for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or bearish.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated reversal patterns (e.g., bullish → bearish → bullish), model often misreads momentum; use sentiment-weighted moving average to smooth out false signals.
